facts.statement: There is no permanent dark side of the Moon. The far side gets as much sunlight as the near side. Like Earth, the Moon has a day side and a night side, which change as it rotates. At new moon it is daytime on the far side (night on the near side); at full moon it is daytime on the near side.
The Earth and Moon are tidally locked, so the same hemisphere of the Moon always faces Earth; the far side is the hemisphere we never see from Earth. Calling it the 'dark side' is misleading.
NASA's EPIC camera on the DSCOVR satellite, about 1 million miles (1.6 million km) from Earth, photographed the fully sunlit far side of the Moon crossing in front of Earth on 16 July 2015.

source.title: From a Million Miles Away, NASA Camera Shows Moon Crossing Face of Earth
